chunks: The high price of goods was mentioned in the presence of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), so he said: 'What concern of mine is its expensiveness? If it is expensive, it is upon Him (God); and if it is cheap, it is upon Him (God).'

key_terms.رَخُصَ: To become cheap, to fall in price
key_terms.عَلَيْهِ: Upon Him — referring to God's authority and control over all things
key_terms.غَلَا: To become expensive, to rise in price
key_terms.غَلَاءُ السِّعْرِ: High prices, inflation — the rising cost of essential goods

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say about high prices and inflation?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) demonstrates complete reliance on God (tawakkul) in the face of economic hardship. When his companions raised the issue of rising prices — a pressing concern for ordinary people in early Islamic society — the Imam redirected their attention from worldly anxiety to divine providence. His words indicate that economic fluctuations are entirely in God's hands, and the believer's duty is trust, not worry.
